table.name: Friend
table.purpose: Friendship edges between high school students: each row states that the student with ID student_id is friends with the student with ID friend_id. Both columns reference Highschooler.ID. Likely from the classic 'social network' schema (with Likes as the other edge table). The pair (student_id, friend_id) presumably forms the key; friendship may be directional as stored (only one row per pair).

friend_id.name: friend_id
friend_id.description: ID of the Highschooler who is the friend in the relationship; references Highschooler.ID (e.g. 1689=Gabriel, 1709=Cassandra, 1934=Kyle).

student_id.name: student_id
student_id.description: ID of the Highschooler who has the friend; references Highschooler.ID (e.g. 1689=Gabriel, 1316=Austin, 1025=John).

table.name: Highschooler
table.purpose: Directory of high school students, one row per student, referenced by the Friend and Likes tables which record friendships and crushes between students.

ID.name: student_id
ID.description: Unique identifier of a high school student; primary key of this table, referenced by Friend.student_id, Friend.friend_id, Likes.student_id and Likes.liked_id.

grade.name: grade_level
grade.description: Student's school grade year, 9-12 (US high school freshman through senior).

name.name: first_name
name.description: Student's first name; not unique (Gabriel and Jordan each appear twice).

table.name: Likes
table.purpose: Edge table recording which high school student likes which other student; each row is a directed 'student X likes student Y' relationship between Highschooler records. Note: student_id is flagged as primary key by statistics, but with only 10 rows and full uniqueness this is likely a sampling artifact; the true key is probably the pair (student_id, liked_id).

liked_id.name: liked_id
liked_id.description: ID of the Highschooler who is liked (the target of the like). References Highschooler.ID.

student_id.name: student_id
student_id.description: ID of the Highschooler who likes someone (the source of the like). References Highschooler.ID. Detected as primary key, but this is likely an artifact of the small sample; the natural key is (student_id, liked_id).
